papers.title: Muon Tridents at FASER and NA64$\mu$: Motivation, Predictions, and Prospects for Precision Measurements
papers.abstract: The intense flux of high-energy muons produced in the far-forward region of $pp$ collisions at the LHC provides a unique opportunity to study rare electromagnetic interactions at TeV energies. In this work, we investigate the muon trident scattering in muon-nucleus interactions at the FASER experiment, which is expected to have recorded more than $10^5$ such events. The theoretical description of the process is reviewed and improved. Predictions for the total event rates and differential distributions expected during Run~3 of the LHC are presented, taking into account realistic detector acceptance and the main background contributions. The dependence of the predictions on the treatment of the nuclear form factors and the impact of higher-order QED effects such as Coulomb corrections are investigated. Our results indicate that the muon trident process can be measured for the first time at TeV energies using FASER's spectrometer, with a projected precision on the cross-section at the percent level. We also extended our analysis to the NA64$\mu$ experiment and showed that, together with FASER, these experiments can probe the energy dependence of the muon trident cross-section over a broad unexplored energy range.
papers.reason: Investigates muon trident scattering in muon-nucleus interactions at FASER and NA64mu with careful treatment of nuclear form factors, highly relevant to neutrino/lepton-nucleus physics. [favorite author: Felix Kling]

summary.tldr: FASER's spectrometer and NA64$\mu$ can perform the first precision, percent-level measurements of coherent muon trident scattering at high energies, revealing significant inaccuracies in current Monte Carlo generator implementations.
summary.novel_idea: The paper demonstrates that FASER can measure coherent muon trident production ($\\mu^\\pm A \\to \\mu^\\pm \\mu^+ \\mu^- A$) at TeV energies using solely its electronic tracking spectrometer and scintillators, bypassing the slower emulsion analysis. It provides the first complete theoretical calculation of muon tridents incorporating realistic Woods-Saxon nuclear form factors, identical-fermion interference, and Coulomb corrections.
summary.method: The authors perform an unapproximated tree-level $2\\to 4$ QED matrix element calculation with FeynCalc, integrated via a dedicated 7-variable Monte Carlo generator for tungsten and lead targets. Full detector acceptance cuts, muon identification criteria, and detailed electromagnetic/hadronic shower background simulations (bremsstrahlung, Bethe-Heitler pair production, and DIS muon misidentification) are modeled for FASER and NA64$\mu$.
key_results: FASER is projected to record $>8.5 \\times 10^4$ coherent muon trident events in Run 3 after acceptance cuts (overall acceptance $\\sim 20\\%$), delivering percent-level statistical precision.
NA64$\\mu$ Phase II (160 GeV beam, $10^{13}$ MOT) is projected to observe $8.8 \\times 10^7$ events, cleanly testing the energy scaling alongside FASER.
Standard event generators deviate substantially at TeV energies: Geant4 and PROPOSAL predict only $\\sim 65\\%$ and $\\sim 25\\%$ of the full cross section, respectively.
Higher-order Coulomb corrections depend non-trivially on beam energy and reduce expected event rates by $1.4\\%$ at FASER and $6.1\\%$ at NA64$\\mu$.
Trident measurements place competitive bounds on $L_\\mu - L_\\tau$ gauge bosons, reaching $g' \\approx 10^{-2}$ at FASER and $4 \\times 10^{-3}$ at NA64$\\mu$ for $m_{Z'} < 0.1\\text{ GeV}$.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly impacts the reader's interest in forward physics facilities (FASER/FPF), lepton-nucleus interactions, and electroweak/QED event generator validation. It establishes muon tridents as a benchmark standard candle for high-energy forward detectors and highlights deficiencies in standard tools like Geant4.
summary.caveats: Relies on purely electronic identification without emulsion vertex reconstruction, requiring strict kinematic cuts to suppress shower backgrounds. The BSM sensitivity projections account only for statistical uncertainties.

papers.title: $\Delta(1232)$ isobars and neutrino opacities in hot dense matter
papers.abstract:
We calculated the diffusion mean free paths of electron neutrinos and antineutrinos in hot, neutrino-trapped matter containing $\Delta(1232)$ isobars, as found in proto-neutron stars and neutron star merger remnants. We included charged-current absorption with the $N\Delta$ weak vertex of weak pion production, neutral-current scattering on all baryons and three-body antineutrino absorption on electron--baryon pairs, with relativistic mean-field kinematics. The reaction $ ar
u_e+e^-+n	o\Delta^-$ dominates the antineutrino opacity whenever the neutron and electron chemical potentials exceed the in-medium $\Delta^-$ rest energy, even where the $\Delta$ population is negligible. At two to four times saturation density, where the reaction is open, it shortens the antineutrino mean free path from 
ubarLamNucMin--
ubarLamNucMax~m to 
ubarLamDMin--
ubarLamDMax~cm. Because antineutrinos are scarce at high lepton fraction, this changes lepton-number diffusion only at low lepton fraction, by up to \DtwoRedHi\% at these densities and by a factor of \DtwoRedLow\ at 1.5 times saturation density. For electron neutrinos, absorption on the $\Delta^-$ and, at low lepton fraction, the opening of nucleonic absorption shorten the mean free path by factors of up to 
uRatioYLthreeMax\ at lepton fraction 0.3 and up to about 
uRatioYLoneMax\ at lepton fraction 0.1. We also showed that, for a given axial coupling, the spin of the $\Delta$ reduces its Gamow--Teller strength per particle from 3 to $5/3$.
papers.reason: Calculates neutrino and antineutrino diffusion mean free paths in hot dense matter including Δ(1232) isobars, directly relevant to core-collapse supernovae and proto-neutron stars.

summary.tldr: The $\\Delta(1232)$ isobar dramatically increases electron-antineutrino opacities in hot, dense proto-neutron star matter through the three-body absorption channel $\\bar{\\nu}_e + e^- + n \\to \\Delta^-$, reducing antineutrino mean free paths from meters to centimeters.
summary.novel_idea: The paper identifies and calculates the three-body antineutrino absorption reaction $\\bar{\\nu}_e + e^- + n \\to \\Delta^-$ in dense matter. It demonstrates that this process opens whenever $\\mu_n + \\mu_e$ exceeds the in-medium $\\Delta^-$ rest energy, dominating antineutrino opacity even in regions where the ambient $\\Delta$ population is virtually zero.
summary.method: Calculations use two relativistic mean-field equations of state (DDME2 and QMC-RMF3) extended with the $\\Delta(1232)$ quartet in $\\beta$-equilibrium with trapped neutrinos. Full Rarita-Schwinger spin-3/2 matrix elements and empirical $N\\Delta$ weak transition form factors are integrated over relativistic phase space using quasi-Monte Carlo techniques, with consistency checks against in-medium $\\Delta^-$ widths and Landau-Migdal parameters for pion condensation stability.
key_results: The reaction $\\bar{\\nu}_e + e^- + n \\to \\Delta^-$ reduces the $\\bar{\\nu}_e$ diffusion mean free path from $3\\text{--}300\\text{ m}$ down to $0.5\\text{--}16\\text{ cm}$ at $(2\\text{--}4)n_0$, representing an opacity jump of 2 to 4 orders of magnitude.

At low lepton fraction ($Y_L = 0.1$), typical of late proto-neutron star deleptonization, the total lepton-number diffusion coefficient is lowered by up to $32\\%$ at $\\ge 2n_0$ and by a factor of $3.0$ at $1.5n_0$.

Analytic derivation of the static limit for spin-3/2 baryons proves that the Gamow-Teller strength per particle is $5/3$ (relative to $g_A^2$), compared to $3$ for nucleons, demonstrating that $\\Delta^-$ scattering is driven primarily by its weak vector charge.

The in-medium width of the produced $\\Delta^-$ is found to be $4.5\\text{--}40\\text{ MeV}$, with the matter remaining stable against $\\pi^-$ condensation provided $g'_{\\Delta\\Delta} \\gtrsim 0.6\\text{--}1.3$.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly links $N \\to \\Delta$ weak transition form factors ($C_5^A$) and resonance kinematics to core-collapse supernova and binary merger neutrino transport. It shows that neutrino transport simulations omitting $\\Delta$ degrees of freedom severely overestimate antineutrino diffusion during late deleptonization.
summary.caveats: Omits dynamical spin-isospin tensor correlations and non-resonant $N\\pi$ continuum contributions; the in-medium $\\Delta$ potential and dispersion relation far above the Fermi surface carry significant theoretical uncertainties.

papers.title: The neutrino fog for inelastic dark matter
papers.abstract: We characterize the behavior of the neutrino fog for inelastic dark matter scattering on xenon. The inelastic scattering kinematics reshape the recoil spectrum of the signal and produce a qualitatively different neutrino fog landscape. In some regions of the inelastic parameter space the fog is completely absent for future xenon experiments at any scale, while in other regions the fog is dispelled only to reappear at larger exposures. We find that multiple background sources with uncertain normalizations can make the onset of the fog jump discontinuously with the dark matter mass and mass splitting, while the discovery limit varies smoothly. We also describe a mechanism by which reduced uncertainties on neutrino rates may have the unintuitive effect of raising neutrino floors derived from the fog opacity.
papers.reason: Characterizes the neutrino fog for inelastic dark matter scattering on xenon, detailing how recoil spectra and backgrounds reshape the discovery limits.

summary.tldr: Inelastic dark matter kinematically shifts nuclear recoils above coherent neutrino-nucleus scattering backgrounds, dispelling the neutrino fog in xenon experiments above mass splittings of $\\sim 180\\text{ keV}$.
summary.novel_idea: The paper maps the neutrino fog for endothermic inelastic dark matter ($m_\\chi \\delta$) in liquid xenon, showing that the fog clears completely well below the kinematic boundary. It also uncovers a statistical anomaly in multi-background environments where tightening neutrino flux uncertainties counterintuitively raises the fog-derived discovery floor.
summary.method: Computes nuclear recoil spectra for inelastic scattering on xenon using WimPyDD for both the Standard Halo Model (SHM) and an LMC high-speed component. A binned profile likelihood ratio test evaluates the discovery limit across 8B, hep, atmospheric, and DSNB CEvNS backgrounds to compute the fog opacity index $n(N) = - (d\\ln\\sigma / d\\ln N)^{-1}$.
key_results: For $m_\\chi = 1\\text{ TeV}$, the neutrino fog ($n > 2$) vanishes completely for splittings $\\delta \\gtrsim 140\\text{ keV}$ up to $10^{10}\\text{ tonne-years}$, and is absent for any mass above $\\delta \\approx 146\\text{ keV}$ (SHM) or $178\\text{ keV}$ (SHM+LMC).

The opacity function $n(N)$ develops a multi-peak structure from distinct neutrino sources, causing the fog-onset threshold to jump discontinuously by orders of magnitude over small variations in $\\delta$ or $m_\\chi$.

Reducing the atmospheric neutrino rate uncertainty from $25\\%$ to $10\\%$ shifts the fog onset to lower exposures, counterintuitively raising the fog-derived cross-section floor by up to a factor of 2 at $\\delta = 120\\text{ keV}$.
summary.why_it_matters: Relevant to the reader's interest in CEvNS as an irreducible background and BSM physics searches. It provides critical context for interpreting high-energy nuclear recoil signals (such as the LZ excess) and highlights structural pitfalls in the standard neutrino fog parameterization.
summary.caveats: Assumes an idealized detector with perfect energy resolution and $100\\%$ efficiency down to sub-keV recoils, neglecting non-neutrino detector backgrounds and Earth orbital modulation.

papers.title: Indication of Electron Antineutrinos from the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background
papers.abstract:
We report an indication of $ ar{
u}_e$ from the diffuse supernova neutrino background (DSNB) based on a spectral fit analysis of a 5003.0-day dataset in Super-Kamiokande. Key improvements over previous searches include enhanced rejection of atmospheric $
u$ backgrounds, updated evaluations of systematic uncertainties, and a refined spectral fitting method. Using a representative DSNB model, the best-fit flux was determined to be $3.6^{+1.6}_{-1.5}~\mathrm{cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$ for $E_
u>13.3$~MeV, corresponding to a $2.6\sigma$ tension with a null hypothesis ($99.5\%$ C.L., one-sided). Similar significances were obtained with signal models of varying spectral shapes.
papers.reason: Reports a 2.6 sigma indication of electron antineutrinos from the diffuse supernova neutrino background using an updated spectral analysis of Super-Kamiokande data. [favorite author: Kate Scholberg]

summary.tldr: Super-Kamiokande reports a $2.6\\sigma$ indication of electron antineutrinos from the diffuse supernova neutrino background using a 5003-day dataset enhanced by gadolinium neutron tagging.
summary.novel_idea: Presents the first experimental indication of the diffuse supernova neutrino background (DSNB) flux, achieved by combining pure-water and gadolinium-loaded phases (SK-IV through SK-VIII) with refined atmospheric background rejection and advanced spectral fitting.
summary.method: Analyzes 5003.0 live-days of inverse beta decay (IBD, $\\bar{\\nu}_e + p \\to e^+ + n$) candidate events with delayed neutron tagging, leveraging Gd concentrations up to $0.033\\%$ (75% capture fraction). A maximum-likelihood spectral fit is conducted over $E_\\nu \\in [13.3, 81.3]\\text{ MeV}$ incorporating six background models (spallation isotopes, neutral-current atmospheric, charged-current atmospheric, reactor, and NC elastic).
key_results: Best-fit DSNB $\\bar{\\nu}_e$ flux of $3.6^{+1.6}_{-1.5}\\text{ cm}^{-2}\\text{ s}^{-1}$ for $E_\\nu > 13.3\\text{ MeV}$ under a representative core-collapse model.
The observed excess excludes the null hypothesis at $2.6\\sigma$ ($99.5\\%$ C.L., one-sided), with similar significance verified across diverse theoretical spectral shapes.
Demonstrates successful operation and neutron background suppression using dissolved $\\mathrm{Gd_2(SO_4)_3 \\cdot 8H_2O}$ across multiple run configurations.
summary.why_it_matters: A landmark experimental result in low-energy neutrino astrophysics and supernova physics (co-authored by Kate Scholberg). The measured flux directly constrains star formation history, cosmic core-collapse rates, and black hole formation fractions, setting the baseline for future DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande low-energy programs.
summary.caveats: Statistical significance remains at the indication level ($2.6\\sigma$), requiring confirmation with further Gd-doped exposure, JUNO, or Hyper-Kamiokande; neutral-current atmospheric background modelling remains a critical systematic uncertainty.

papers.title: Subthreshold Resonances in the Scattering of {\mu}^-Mesons by Atomic Nuclei
papers.abstract: A theoretical study of pre-threshold resonant excitation of atomic nuclei is presented. A formalism for utilizing leptonic probes in the energy region of a Feshbach-Baz pre-threshold resonance is proposed. The resonance positions and widths are shown to be intrinsically linked to the nuclear structure parameters. The correspondence of the giant dipole resonance (GDR) region for heavy nuclei to low probe energies, as well as its large resonance widths, is demonstrated. Through this framework, free from the intense background, the observable signatures of GDR excitation and de-excitation channels, including nuclear fission, are predicted
papers.reason: Studies pre-threshold resonant excitation of atomic nuclei using leptonic probes and evaluates giant dipole resonance channels, sitting squarely in low-energy lepton-nucleus physics.

summary.tldr: Subthreshold Feshbach-Baz resonances in low-energy negative muon-nucleus scattering can resonantly excite nuclear giant dipole resonances, offering a clean, background-free probe of radiative widths and nuclear de-excitation.
summary.novel_idea: The paper adapts Feshbach-Baz pre-threshold resonance theory to leptonic scattering, showing that incident $\\mu^-$ with kinetic energies below the nuclear excitation threshold can form quasi-bound mesoatom states that resonantly excite nuclear giant dipole resonances (GDR) without photon backgrounds.
summary.method: The authors solve radial Schrödinger equations for muonic bound and continuum states in a finite-size, uniformly charged spherical nuclear potential. Partial-wave expansion links the elastic resonance width $\\Gamma_{el}$ in the P-wave directly to experimental $E1$ photon absorption widths $\\Gamma_\\gamma$ via dipole matrix elements.
key_results: Single-particle $E1$ transitions in lighter nuclei yield tiny relative widths ($\\Gamma / E_{res} \\sim 10^{-6}\\text{--}10^{-8}$), making them impractical for current beam resolutions.

For heavy actinide nuclei ($^{232}\\text{Th}$, $^{235}\\text{U}$, $^{238}\\text{U}$), GDR excitations match incident muon energies of $1.7\\text{--}2.1\\text{ MeV}$ with relative widths $\\Gamma_{EM}/E_{res} \\approx 0.015\\text{--}0.020$, accessible with percent-level beam resolutions.
Resonant electromagnetic cross sections reach $3.5\\text{--}4.5\\text{ barns}$, providing an experimental path to measure direct GDR gamma decay and photofission free of bremsstrahlung background.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides an interesting electromagnetic perspective on nuclear excitation and de-excitation channels (relevant to nuclear remnants and gamma cascades), though tangential to primary neutrino interaction workflows.
summary.caveats: Relies on an idealized uniformly charged spherical nucleus; GDR collective modes are treated via an average Lorentzian approximation rather than microscopic RPA or spectral functions; negative muon beams of requisite intensity and energy spread are currently challenging to realize.

papers.title: Nucleon polarizabilities revisited: insights from the Bernab\'eu-Ericson-Ferro Fontan-Tarrach sum rule
papers.abstract: We present a complete dispersive evaluation of the Bernab\'eu-Ericson-Ferro Fontan-Tarrach (BEFT) sum rule for the nucleon dipole polarizability difference $\alpha_{E1}-\beta_{M1}$. The analysis is based on hyperbolic dispersion relations, which separate the $s$- and $t$-channel contributions without double counting and are particularly suited to backward real Compton scattering. This framework makes it possible to precisely determine the polarizability difference from independent dispersive input rather than from fits to low-energy Compton scattering data. The $s$-channel part is updated with modern single-pion photoproduction multipoles and model estimates of non-$\pi N$ inelastic channels. For the $t$-channel, we use contemporary dispersive input for $\gamma\gamma\to\pi\pi/K\bar K_{I_t=0}$ together with Roy-Steiner equation solutions for $\pi\pi/K\bar K_{I_t=0}\to N\bar N$, and we extend the calculation to the isovector $\pi\eta/K\bar K_{I_t=1}$ channel associated with the $a_0(980)$. The resulting treatment resolves the long-standing puzzle of earlier BEFT evaluations driven by the scalar-isoscalar two-pion channel and gives a controlled estimate of the subleading isovector contribution. Combining the resulting BEFT values with the Baldin sum rule, we obtain, in units of $10^{-4}\,\mathrm{fm}^3$, \[ \alpha_{E1}^p=11.17(52),\quad \beta_{M1}^p=2.84(52),\quad \alpha_{E1}^n=12.18(59),\quad \beta_{M1}^n=3.03(59). \] For the proton, these values provide a benchmark with a precision comparable to state-of-the-art dispersive and chiral effective field theory extractions. For the neutron, whose polarizabilities are much less directly constrained experimentally, the result provides an independent dispersive benchmark with an uncertainty comparable to that of the proton.
papers.topic: Nucleon Polarizabilities and BEFT Sum Rule
papers.reason: Performs a complete dispersive evaluation of the Bernabeu-Ericson-Ferro Fontan-Tarrach sum rule for nucleon polarizabilities using modern pion photoproduction and Roy-Steiner inputs, highly relevant to nucleon structure.

summary.tldr: A complete dispersive evaluation of the BEFT sum rule for nucleon dipole polarizabilities resolves long-standing scalar-isoscalar puzzles and provides independent benchmarks.
summary.novel_idea: The paper provides the first complete, modern dispersive evaluation of the Bernabéu-Ericson-Ferro Fontan-Tarrach (BEFT) sum rule using hyperbolic dispersion relations, systematically extending the calculation to include the isovector $\piceil/K\bar{K}$ channel associated with the $a_0(980)$ resonance.
summary.method: The framework utilizes hyperbolic dispersion relations for backward real Compton scattering to avoid double counting between $s$ - and $t$ -channels. The $s$ -channel is updated with modern SAID single-pion photoproduction multipoles, while the $t$ -channel incorporates Roy-Steiner equation solutions for $\pi\pi/K\bar{K}$ and chiral perturbation theory for isovector states.
key_results: Proton static polarizabilities: $\alpha_{E1}^p = 11.17(52)$ and $\beta_{M1}^p = 2.84(52)$ in units of $10^{-4}\;\mathrm{fm}^3$.
Neutron static polarizabilities: $\alpha_{E1}^n = 12.18(59)$ and $\beta_{M1}^n = 3.03(59)$ in units of $10^{-4}\;\mathrm{fm}^3$.
Resolves the historical discrepancy in the $t$ -channel $S$-wave $\pi\pi$ contribution between Holstein-Nathan and Drechsel et al. extractions.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides crucial precision inputs and data-driven constraints on nucleon polarizabilities and electromagnetic mass differences, highly relevant to low-energy nuclear matrix elements and precision electroweak calculations.
summary.caveats: Uncertainties are dominated by the $t$ -channel cutoffs and dispersive model inputs, and full crossed-channel treatments for kaon systems are left for future work.

papers.title: Two-Pion Exchange Paradigm in Hadron-Hadron Interactions from Lattice QCD
papers.abstract: We study hadron-hadron interactions in (2+1)-flavor lattice QCD near the physical pion mass ($m_\pi \simeq 146\mathrm{MeV}$) using the HAL QCD method, with particular emphasis on two-pion exchange (TPE). The nucleon--flavor-singlet hadron potentials such as $\phi$-$N$, $J/\psi$-$N$, and $\eta_c$-$N$ are found to be attractive at all distances. Moreover, in the long-range region where one-pion exchange is forbidden, we observe lattice signatures consistent with TPE dominance. These results demonstrate that the HAL QCD method can extract universal long-distance phenomena, such as TPE, directly from nonperturbative QCD dynamics.
papers.reason: Applies the HAL QCD method near the physical pion mass to study hadron-hadron potentials, finding universal lattice signatures of two-pion exchange dominance.

summary.tldr: HAL QCD lattice simulations near the physical pion mass demonstrate that two-pion exchange dominates long-range hadron-hadron potentials.
summary.novel_idea: Provides direct nonperturbative lattice QCD evidence at $m_pi \simeq 146$ MeV that two-pion exchange (TPE) governs the long-range behavior of interactions between flavor-singlet hadrons and nucleons where one-pion exchange is forbidden.
summary.method: Applies the HAL QCD method to (2+1)-flavor gauge configurations with $a = 0.0846$ fm and $V = (8.12\;\mathrm{fm})^3$, evaluating spatial effective energies to extract $\phi-N$, $J/\psi-N$, and $\eta_c-N$ potentials.
key_results: Potentials for $\phi-N$, $J/\psi-N$, and $\eta_c-N$ are attractive across all inter-hadron distances in the $S$-wave channels.
The spatial effective energy $E_{m eff}(r)$ exhibits a clear plateau near $2m_pi \simeq 292.8$ MeV for $r \gtrsim 1.0$ fm, signaling TPE dominance.
Supports the existence of charmonium-nucleus bound states through attractive in-medium mass shifts.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly links lattice QCD dynamics to chiral EFT frameworks of two-pion exchange and nuclear forces, relevant for understanding nonperturbative hadron interactions and exotic hadronic matter.
summary.caveats: High statistical uncertainties in long-range tails require larger lattice statistics, and contributions from higher-order chiral diagrams like the $\pi\pi NN$ seagull term need further quantification.

papers.title: Dilepton azimuthal anisotropy from coherent $J/\psi$ photoproduction in hadronic Pb-Pb collisions
papers.abstract: Hadron-based event-plane estimators can be affected by nonflow and autocorrelation biases, especially at low multiplicity. Coherent $J/\psi$ photoproduction offers a complementary geometry reference through the correlation between quasireal-photon polarization and the reaction plane. We calculate the second-order dilepton coefficient $A_2$ relative to the reaction plane in hadronic Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.36$ TeV within an equivalent-photon and generalized vector-meson-dominance Glauber framework. Nuclear diffraction and two-source interference produce a pronounced transverse-momentum dependence, while the rapidity dependence is weak. We also compare two treatments of coherent scattering in the overlap region of the two colliding nuclei. Suppressing the contribution from this region reduces the yield and strengthens the integrated polarization--reaction-plane correlation, with the largest differences in central and semicentral collisions and smaller differences toward peripheral collisions. Joint measurements of the coherent yield and $A_2$ can constrain how hadronic interactions disrupt nuclear coherence and clarify the photoproduction mechanism. With sufficient tagged yields, azimuthal correlations involving decay leptons from photoproduced $J/\psi$ mesons could complement studies of collectivity, with potential future applications to small systems.
papers.reason: Calculates the second-order dilepton coefficient from coherent J/psi photoproduction in hadronic Pb-Pb collisions, directly touching upon nuclear shadowing, vector-meson dominance, and Glauber frameworks.

summary.tldr: Dilepton azimuthal anisotropies from coherent $J/\psi$ photoproduction in Pb-Pb collisions provide a sensitive geometry reference for heavy-ion collisions.
summary.novel_idea: Demonstrates that the second-order dilepton coefficient $A_2$ relative to the reaction plane, driven by quasireal photon polarization, can map nuclear overlap geometry and constrain interference effects without hadronic nonflow biases.
summary.method: Calculates the yield and $A_2$ for coherent $J/\psi$ photoproduction in $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 5.36$ TeV Pb-Pb collisions using an equivalent-photon and generalized VMD-Glauber framework, comparing $N+N$ and $N+S$ overlap prescriptions.
key_results: In the long-wavelength limit $p_{\mathrm{T}} \to 0$, $A_2$ approaches $-1/4$, indicating complete polarization alignment with the impact parameter.
Suppressing the overlap contribution in the $N+S$ prescription reduces the yield and strengthens the magnitude of integrated $A_2$ compared to $N+N$.
Two-source interference alters the vector structure and suppresses $|A_2|$ over broad momentum intervals while leaving the integrated yield nearly constant.
summary.why_it_matters: Offers a novel electromagnetic probe of collision geometry and coherence in heavy-ion collisions, complementing standard hadronic event-plane estimators and shedding light on low-$p_{\mathrm{T}}$ $J/\psi$ production mechanisms.
summary.caveats: Calculations neglect subsequent in-medium dissociation and regeneration, and direct comparisons to experimental data require matching precise experimental lepton acceptances and event-plane resolutions.

papers.title: Revisiting supernova constraints on dark gauge bosons
papers.abstract: We revisit the supernova constraints on three well-motivated light gauge bosons: the dark photon, the $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge boson, and the $U(1)_{L_\mu-L_\tau}$ gauge boson. For the dark photon and the $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge boson, we re-evaluate the nucleon bremsstrahlung process within the one-pion exchange approximation, retaining the full momentum and mass dependence. The geometrical dependence of the decay and absorption of these gauge bosons inside the supernova core is also taken into account. Updated bounds on these models are derived based on the cooling of SN1987A and energy deposition constraints from low-energy supernovae (LESNe). Taking the SFHo-18.8 $18.8\,M_\odot$ profile, the SN1987A cooling constraints reach masses of about $230$ MeV, $280$ MeV, and $300$ MeV for the dark photon, the $U(1)_{B-L}$ boson, and the $U(1)_{L_\mu-L_\tau}$ boson, while the corresponding LESN limits extend to about $450$ MeV, $440$ MeV, and $600$ MeV, respectively. The kinetic mixing parameter $\epsilon$ for dark photon, the gauge coupling $g_{BL}$ in the $U(1)_{B-L}$ model, and the gauge coupling $g_{\mu\tau}$ for the $U(1)_{L_\mu-L_\tau}$ model are constrained down to $5.8\times10^{-12}$, $2.9\times10^{-16}$, and $6.4\times10^{-12}$, respectively.
papers.reason:
Revisits supernova constraints on dark photons, B-L, and L_
u-L_	au gauge bosons using realistic nucleon bremsstrahlung and SN1987A/LESN cooling bounds.

summary.tldr: Updated SN1987A cooling and low-energy supernova limits constrain light dark gauge bosons using full momentum-dependent nucleon bremsstrahlung.
summary.novel_idea: Re-evaluates nucleon bremsstrahlung production of dark photons and $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge bosons using the one-pion exchange approximation with full momentum and mass dependence, incorporating in-medium plasma effects and stellar geometry.
summary.method: Computes energy emission rates in transverse and longitudinal modes by integrating over realistic supernova profiles (Fischer $11.8M_\odot$, SFHo-18.8 $M_\odot$, and LS220 $20M_\odot$) while accounting for core absorption and mantle energy deposition.
key_results: SN1987A cooling bounds exclude $Z^{\prime}$ masses up to $280$ MeV and gauge couplings $g_{BL}$ down to $2.9 \times 10^{-16}$ in longitudinal modes for the SFHo-18.8 profile.
Low-energy supernova (LESN) energy deposition constraints extend mass exclusions up to $450$ MeV for dark photons and $440$ MeV for $U(1)_{B-L}$ bosons.
For $U(1)_{L_\mu-L_\tau}$ gauge bosons produced via neutrino coalescence and semi-Compton scattering, masses up to $600$ MeV and couplings down to $6.4 \times 10^{-12}$ are excluded.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides rigorous, up-to-date astrophysical constraints on sub-GeV dark sector mediators, directly relevant for BSM phenomenology at neutrino and intensity-frontier facilities.
summary.caveats: Results depend moderately on uncertainties in nuclear equations of state, core temperature profiles, and the approximations inherent to the one-pion exchange framework.

papers.title: Threshold effects of inelastic neutrino-dark-matter scattering in AGN spikes
papers.abstract: High-energy neutrinos from active galactic nuclei provide a powerful probe of dark matter (DM) spikes surrounding supermassive black holes. While elastic neutrino-DM scattering mediated by a light particle produces little net attenuation due to regeneration, inelastic scattering, $\nu\chi_1\to\nu\chi_2$, introduces a nonzero minimum energy loss, $E_{\rm th}$. We show that this threshold prevents the near-cancellation between attenuation and regeneration, producing a distinctive spectral deficit above $E_{\rm th}$ accompanied by a pile-up below it. Solving the full neutrino cascade, including repeated scattering and secondary neutrinos from excited-state decays, we demonstrate that this feature persists for both narrow and broad energy-transfer kernels. Using public IceCube data for NGC 1068 and an unbinned likelihood analysis with a freely fitted intrinsic power-law spectrum, we derive upper limits on the asymptotic optical depth of $\tau_0<26-39$ for a narrow kernel (kernel width $\epsilon=0.01$) over $E_{\rm th}=0.24-3.0$ TeV and $\tau_0<20-26$ for a broad kernel ($\epsilon=0.36$) over $E_{\rm th}=0.24-2.4$ TeV, at the nominal $90\%$ confidence level. An intrinsic high-energy cutoff weakens the narrow-kernel limits by factors of $2.2-7.4$ and the broad-kernel limits by factors of $2.0-5.0$. We further investigate DM velocity effects and combine NGC 1068 with CGCG 420-015 and TXS 0506+056 to extend the threshold reach. In a vector-mediator realization, an optimistic adiabatic DM spike can yield constraints on the neutrino coupling competitive with laboratory bounds for broad energy-transfer kernels.
papers.reason: Analyzes threshold effects of inelastic neutrino-dark-matter scattering in AGN spikes using IceCube data, blending high-energy neutrino astronomy with dark matter models.

summary.tldr: Inelastic neutrino-dark-matter scattering in AGN spikes introduces a kinematic energy-loss threshold, creating distinctive spectral deficits and pile-ups in IceCube data.
summary.novel_idea: Shows that a nonzero minimum energy loss $E_{\text{th}}$ in inelastic neutrino-DM scattering prevents the near-cancellation between attenuation and regeneration seen in elastic models, yielding a pronounced spectral edge observable by IceCube.
summary.method: Solves the full neutrino cascade including repeated scatterings, secondary decays, and DM velocity distributions, and derives upper limits on asymptotic optical depth $\tau_0$ using unbinned profile-likelihood analyses of IceTracks-DR2 data for NGC 1068.
key_results: For a narrow kernel ($\epsilon = 0.01$), 90% CL limits reach $\tau_0 < 26-39$ over $E_{\text{th}} = 0.24-3.0$ TeV for NGC 1068.
For a broad kernel ($\epsilon = 0.36$), constraints strengthen to $\tau_0 < 20-26$ over $E_{\text{th}} = 0.24-2.4$ TeV.
An intrinsic high-energy spectral cutoff weakens these limits by factors of 2.0 to 7.4 depending on kernel width and threshold.
summary.why_it_matters: Connects high-energy astrophysical neutrino observations from active galactic nuclei to particle physics models of inelastic dark matter, providing competitive constraints on dark-sector couplings.
summary.caveats: Constraints are subject to astrophysical uncertainties in the supermassive black hole dark matter spike profile and rely on the astrophysical origin of the neutrino excesses.

papers.title: Lepton polarization and sensitivity to the form factors in $\Lambda\to p\,\ell^-\bar\nu_\ell$ with lattice QCD
papers.abstract: We investigate the polarization of the charged lepton in the semileptonic hyperon decay $\Lambda\to p\,\ell^-\bar\nu_\ell$ ($\ell=e,\mu$) within the Standard Model, using the form factors obtained from lattice QCD. We compute the longitudinal, transverse and normal polarization of the lepton, the forward-backward asymmetry of each lepton spin state, and the lepton flavor universality ratio $R_{\mu e}$. We show that the longitudinal polarization determines the ratio $g_1/f_1$ of the axial-vector to vector couplings, and that the forward-backward asymmetries of the electron and of negative-helicity muons determine the weak magnetism. The asymmetry of positive-helicity muons is fixed by kinematics up to a small dependence on the second-class form factors, whereas $R_{\mu e}$ is nearly independent of $g_1/f_1$ and the weak magnetism. For comparison, we also use the QCD sum-rule form factors, whose $g_1/f_1$ and weak magnetism are opposite in sign to experiment and lattice QCD, and find very different values for the observables that depend on them. Moreover, the $q^2$ dependence of $R_{\mu e}$ fixes the longitudinal polarization of the muon, which can thus be measured from the decay rates, without measuring the muon spin. The normal polarization is generated by the electromagnetic final-state interaction and provides the Standard Model reference for searches for time-reversal violation. The electron forward-backward asymmetry and $R_{\mu e}$ can be measured at BESIII and the proposed Super Tau-Charm Facility, and $R_{\mu e}$ also at LHCb. These measurements can test the Standard Model and the lattice-QCD form factors.
papers.reason: Investigates lepton polarization, form factors, and LFU ratios in semileptonic hyperon decays (Ε→pℓ̄͵̄͵) using lattice QCD inputs.

papers.title: Finite-temperature ab-initio-Informed Nuclear Equation-of-State Tables (FINEST): Nuclear matter uncertainties in core-collapse supernovae
papers.abstract: We construct new finite-temperature, composition-dependent equation of state (EOS) tables for astrophysical simulations by implementing a recently developed energy-density functional. The functional is constrained by ab initio nuclear matter calculations and neutron-star observations. A distinguishing feature of this functional is a non-monotonic density dependence of the nucleon effective mass, with an increase beyond saturation density. Using these EOS tables, we investigate the impact of current uncertainties in nuclear matter properties on core-collapse supernova (CCSN) evolution with spherically symmetric simulations employing an effective treatment of convective mixing. The magnitude of the EOS effects depends on the progenitor compactness. Within current constraints, variations in incompressibility, symmetry energy, and high-density pressure produce only modest differences during the early post-bounce evolution. In contrast, the effective mass dependence has a much stronger influence on proto-neutron star contraction and the explosion dynamics in a stellar model with high core compactness. Its non-monotonic density dependence leads to a qualitatively different contraction history and can alter the explosion outcome compared to mean-field effective-mass behaviors. Therefore, among the nuclear matter properties considered, the density dependence of the nucleon effective masses has by far the largest impact on CCSN dynamics. This highlights the importance of realistic effective-mass parameterizations in nuclear EOSs used in astrophysical simulations.
papers.reason: Constructs ab-initio-informed finite-temperature nuclear equation-of-state tables and investigates nuclear matter uncertainties and nucleon effective masses in core-collapse supernovae.

papers.title: Nuclear recoil effects with a realistic nuclear charge form factor
papers.abstract: We introduce a novel two-parameter Gamma model of the nuclear charge distribution as an alternative to the widely used Fermi distribution. The model yields simple analytical formulas for all moments of the charge distribution and closed-form expressions for the electrostatic potential and momentum-space form factor, the latter satisfying the correct analyticity requirements for a physical charged particle. We apply the model to calculate the nuclear recoil correction to the Lamb shift in electronic and muonic atoms and analyze its nuclear-model dependence. We find that the nuclear-size recoil corrections to energy levels of heavy muonic atoms are strongly sensitive to higher moments of the nuclear charge distribution, highlighting the importance of realistic nuclear modeling. To facilitate further calculations, we also provide the Fortran code RECFNS, designed for computing the nuclear recoil correction within the QED framework. The present work establishes a basis for future extensions to higher orders in the electron-to-nucleus mass ratio, hyperfine splitting, and radiative corrections.
papers.topic: Nuclear recoil and charge form factor
papers.reason: Introduces a Gamma model for nuclear charge distributions and calculates nuclear recoil corrections to atomic Lamb shifts, emphasizing realistic nuclear modeling.

papers.title: Probing Orbital Angular Momentum Distributions in Elastic Vector Meson Production in Longitudinally Polarized Electron--Proton Scattering
papers.abstract: We consider elastic vector meson production in longitudinally polarized electron-proton collisions at small $x$. Inspired by previous pioneering proposals in the literature, we calculate the numerator of the longitudinal double-spin asymmetry (DSA) within the polarized small-$x$ formalism for both the transversely and longitudinally polarized vector mesons. Our calculation demonstrates that the $\cos\phi_{k\Delta}$ azimuthal harmonic of the DSA for the elastic vector meson production at small transverse momentum transfer (with $\phi_{k\Delta}$ the azimuthal angle between the transverse momenta of the outgoing electron and meson in the dipole/Trento frame) provides a promising probe of the orbital angular momentum (OAM) distributions at small $x$. Our results can be applied to several different vector meson species, thus opening up a new class of observables that can be used to extract OAM distributions from experimental data.
papers.topic: OAM Distributions in Vector Meson Production
papers.reason: Calculates the longitudinal double-spin asymmetry in elastic vector meson production to probe parton orbital angular momentum, aligning well with electron scattering and GPD interests.

papers.title: Ubiquity of ocular resonances in scattering phenomena
papers.abstract: We demonstrate how quantum mechanical scattering off a potential with a characteristic surface generically leads to a family of resonances in the complex momentum plane clustered near a roughly eye-shaped curve centered on the origin and formed by anti-Stokes lines. A particularly interesting class are potentials that are more singular than $1/r^2$ at short distance, where the scattering surface is the separatrix between captured and deflected classical trajectories. These resonances have been recently shown to play an important role in low energy nucleon scattering, and can be related to ``creeping waves'' familiar from classical diffractive scattering and analyzed by means of Regge poles.
papers.reason: Analyzes universal eye-shaped clusters of quantum resonances in scattering off characteristic potentials, connecting directly to low-energy nucleon scattering.

papers.title: Constraining Nuclear Matter from Finite Nuclei: the Ab Initio Perspective
papers.abstract: This review surveys recent developments in ab initio calculations of finite nuclei aimed at constraining the nuclear matter equation of state. Particular emphasis is placed on observables that connect finite-nucleus structure to bulk properties of nuclear matter, including neutron-skin thicknesses, electric dipole polarizabilities, and monopole sum rules. We discuss how neutron skins and dipole polarizabilities provide information on the density dependence of the symmetry energy, while monopole observables constrain the incompressibility of nuclear matter.
papers.topic: Constraining Nuclear Matter from Ab Initio Calculations
papers.reason: Surveys ab initio calculations of finite nuclei and connects them to bulk nuclear matter properties, symmetry energy, and neutron skins, directly overlapping with nuclear structure interests.

papers.title: Nucleon tomography from a calibrated diquark spectator model
papers.abstract: Generalized parton distributions (GPDs) provide a unified description of the longitudinal-momentum and transverse spatial structure of the nucleon. We calculate the twist-2 vector GPDs $H^{q}$ and $E^{q}$ in a spectator model containing both scalar and axial-vector diquark configurations. A central new result is the explicit analytic expression for the axial-vector-diquark contribution to the helicity-flip GPD $E^{q}$. To regulate the transverse-momentum integrations while retaining a physically sensible dependence on the momentum transfer, we introduce a momentum-transfer-dependent quasi-hard cutoff. The model parameters are determined through two complementary calibrations: one using proton observables only and another simultaneously including proton and neutron observables. Electromagnetic moments and radii, together with selected constraints on gravitational form factors, determine the quark and diquark masses, the relative scalar and axial-vector contributions, and the transverse-momentum scale. The two calibrations yield compatible parameter ranges, while the inclusion of neutron observables reduces the parameter uncertainties and more strongly constrains the flavor structure. From the resulting zero-skewness GPDs $H^{u,d}(x,0,t)$ and $E^{u,d}(x,0,t)$, we calculate the valence-quark PDFs and the impact-parameter distributions of unpolarized up and down quarks in both unpolarized and transversely polarized nucleons. The transverse distributions exhibit the expected localization of large-$x$ quarks near the transverse center of momentum and a flavor-dependent distortion when the nucleon is transversely polarized. Our results provide a unified phenomenological description of the longitudinal-momentum and transverse-position structure of valence quarks in the nucleon.
papers.reason: Calculates twist-2 vector generalized parton distributions (GPDs) in a spectator model with scalar and axial-vector diquarks, providing explicit analytic expressions for helicity-flip GPDs.

papers.title: The Pion Parton Distribution Puzzle in the High x Region
papers.abstract: We developed a new theoretical approach in the description of partonic structure of hadrons based on spectral function representation of valence quarks. In this approach massless valence quarks are considered in the mean field of residual hadron. This approach initially was applied to the calculation of parton distribution function~(PDF) of nucleons that resulted in an observation of pion-cloud structure of nucleon. In this report we present our calculation of pion PDF in the valence region within the same approach. In this approach we describe the soft partonic structure of pion through the valence $q\bar q$ cluster, embedded in the residual field of the pion. The pion PDF is calculated using phenomenological Light-Front wave functions for the $q\bar q$ cluster and the residual field. Our result indicates that the peak position of the x weighted valence PDF~(xPDF) depends on parameters characterizing the virtuality of the $q\bar q$ cluster and the mass of the residual system. These parameters are evaluated by fitting the calculated PDF to the height and the peak position of empirical pion xPDF at starting $Q_0$. They indicate that unlike the nucleon case, very little residual mass is needed in the pion to describe existing pion PDFs in the valence region. They also require the $q\bar q$-cluster to be highly virtual with the interacting quark carrying almost all of the momentum of the $q\bar q$ cluster. This picture is consistent with the dominance of the Feynman mechanism leaving little room for the hard component in the PDF. The calculation practically describes the $\sim (1-x)$ behavior observed recently at $x\to 1$ limit. Our non-trivial observation is that the height and the peak position of xPDF define the analytic behavior of valence PDF at $x\to 1$ limit.
papers.reason: Develops a spectral function approach for valence quarks to calculate the pion parton distribution function, directly relevant to hadron structure and parton dynamics.

papers.title: Probing the Collins effect at photon-photon colliders
papers.abstract: We propose to study the Collins effect in the production of almost back-to-back unpolarized hadrons (mainly charged pions) by looking at their azimuthal distributions around the jet thrust-axis in the process $\gamma\gamma \to h_1h_2X$. The quasi-real photons in the initial state can be emitted either by two scattering leptons or two charged heavy nuclei in ultra-peripheral collisions. We provide numerical estimates for kinematic configurations in principle accessible at the Future Circular Collider and at the planned experiments on ultra-peripheral collisions at the LHC. We find that the corresponding asymmetries can be sizable, even up to around 10-15%. The proposed measurements would thus shed light on the fragmentation mechanism of quarks into hadrons and, in principle, would allow one to distinguish among different existing models for the Collins functions.
papers.reason: Investigates the Collins effect in unpolarized hadron production via photon-photon collisions, providing useful inputs for fragmentation and electron/photon scattering constraints.

papers.title: Neutrino Phenomenology and Leptogenesis from Non-Invertible Fusion Symmetry
papers.abstract: We constructed a minimal type-I seesaw model with two right-handed neutrinos, in which the flavor structure is determined by a non-invertible \(\mathbb{Z}_2\)-gauged \(\mathbb{Z}_5\) fusion symmetry~($\mathbb{Z}^{IN}_5$). The framework, incorporating a second Higgs doublet and an auxiliary \(\mathbb{Z}_2\) parity, yields predictive neutrino mass textures without introducing flavon fields. A fit to neutrino data selects the inverted mass ordering with \(m_3=0\) and predicts a nearly maximal Dirac CP phase, together with a characteristic prediction for the effective Majorana mass governing neutrinoless double-beta decay($0\nu\beta\beta$). We further investigate thermal leptogenesis and show that the framework can reproduce the observed baryon asymmetry of the Universe. Our results establish a connection between predictive neutrino phenomenology and leptogenesis within a minimal framework based on non-invertible fusion symmetry.
papers.reason: Constructs a type-I seesaw model with flavor structure dictated by a non-invertible fusion symmetry, predicting neutrino mass textures and leptogenesis.

papers.title: Valence-quark-core and meson-cloud effects on electromagnetic form factors of $\Delta$ baryons
papers.abstract: Electromagnetic form factors and electromagnetic properties of $\Delta$ baryons are studied in the perturbative chiral quark model (PCQM) using quark wavefunctions predetermined from proton charge form factor data. Our predictions agree reasonably with lattice-QCD and other phenomenological results. For charged $\Delta^{++}$, $\Delta^{+}$, and $\Delta^{-}$, observables are dominated by the three-quark core, with small meson-cloud corrections superimposed. For neutral $\Delta^{0}$, the leading-order quark core contribution vanishes, so meson-cloud corrections fully determine its electromagnetic response. The PCQM gives a nonzero magnetic moment, a negative charge radius, and a sizable magnetic radius for $\Delta^{0}$. This work provides consistent, parameter-free predictions for $\Delta$ baryon structure and highlights the role of meson cloud fluctuations.
papers.reason: Studies electromagnetic form factors and properties of Delta baryons using a chiral quark model and meson cloud effects, directly relevant to nucleon and baryon structure.

papers.title: Large-$N$ $\pi^+\pi^+$ scattering from twisted Eguchi--Kawai reduction
papers.abstract: We present the first computation of the $\pi^+\pi^+$ scattering length in large-$N$ QCD in the 't Hooft limit, $N_{\scriptscriptstyle{\rm f}}/N\to 0$, using the twisted Eguchi--Kawai formulation of the lattice theory. We employ values of $N$ up to 1156 and consider several quark masses and lattice spacings to achieve controlled large-$N$, continuum, and chiral limits. The chiral behavior of the scattering length is compared with next-to-leading-order Chiral Perturbation Theory predictions. Our result for the low-energy coupling describing the sub-leading quark-mass dependence is consistent with existing S-matrix bootstrap bounds. Combining TEK results with previous lattice QCD data obtained using standard methods for $3\le N\le 6$, we are also able to extract sub-leading $\mathcal{O}(1/N)$ corrections to the large-$N$ scattering length.
papers.reason: Computes the large-N pion-pion scattering length using twisted Eguchi-Kawai lattice formulations, testing chiral perturbation theory bounds.

papers.title: The design and flight of the Payload for Ultrahigh Energy Observations (PUEO)
papers.abstract: Sources of cosmic rays at ultrahigh energies (UHE, $\gtrsim$ 1 EeV) are anticipated to give rise to neutrinos at similar energies by production via propagation interactions either within the source region or on cosmological scales. Measurements of the neutrino flux, flavor, and energy provide significant insight into those underlying processes governing UHE cosmic ray acceleration and propagation. Detecting neutrinos at these energies requires immense detector volumes due to their low predicted flux. We present the balloon-borne mission PUEO (Payload for Ultrahigh Energy Observations) which is an antenna array designed to detect the Askaryan emission from UHE neutrino interactions in the Antarctic ice. This paper reports on the design considerations and implementations for constructing PUEO, from the design parameters to the as-built validations.
papers.reason: Presents the design and flight configuration of the PUEO balloon-borne payload for detecting ultrahigh-energy Askaryan neutrino emissions in Antarctic ice.

papers.title: A Low Scale for Quark-Lepton Unification
papers.abstract: The measured fermion masses may be pointing to the scale of quark-lepton unification. Studying the renormalization-group evolution of the Standard Model Yukawa couplings, we find that $y_\tau=y_b$ and $y_\mu=3y_s$ occur at nearly the same scale, around $10^6$ GeV, while the first generation reaches the Georgi-Jarlskog relation $y_e\simeq y_d/3$ at order $10^8$ GeV and can arise from the same Clebsch structure through a simple hierarchical flavor texture. This pattern naturally suggests low-scale Pati-Salam symmetry. We show that flavor mixing and finite threshold corrections preserve this picture. If the electron mass has an independent origin, the two heavier-generation relations can be realized in theories with a unification scale as low as $(5$-$7)\times10^5$ GeV. We identify two simple theories that accommodate all three relations and in which the measured masses fix the flavor structure. The first unifies all three generations at $4.6^{+1.2}_{-0.9}\times10^6$ GeV; the second, with symmetric Yukawa matrices, at $1.5^{+0.7}_{-0.5}\times10^7$ GeV, and predicts $|V_{cb}|=0.042\pm0.002$. Their shared light-family texture fixes the relevant vector-leptoquark couplings, making $\mu\to e$ conversion in nuclei a direct test of unification: upcoming searches will probe part of the region selected by the two theories, and proposed facilities could cover it completely.
papers.reason: Examines low-scale Pati-Salam unification and relates fermion masses to lepton flavor violation probes such as mu-to-e conversion in nuclei.

papers.title: Soft factor of quasi-TMDPDFs from the soft limit of the quasi beam function
papers.abstract: The quasi-TMDPDF in large-momentum effective theory is related to the TMDPDF through a soft factor, which has so far been constructed separately from the quasi beam function. We show that the soft factor is contained in the quasi beam function itself. Computing the one-loop quasi beam function and decomposing it by the method of regions, we find that the hard and collinear regions give the matching coefficient and the lightcone beam function. The soft region involves only one lightlike direction, yet, once the two hemispheres of the gluon momentum are folded onto each other, it reproduces the square root of the lightcone soft function together with the reduced soft function. The analysis leads to an operator definition of the soft factor, as the vacuum matrix element of the soft Wilson lines into which the quasi beam function turns. This definition provides the basis for an all-order analysis, and it shows that the Collins-Soper kernel is reproduced to all orders.
papers.reason: Derives the operator definition of the soft factor for quasi-TMDPDFs from the soft limit of the quasi beam function, relevant to large-momentum effective theory applications.

papers.title: Remembering Brown-Rho scaling
papers.abstract: The properties of hadrons in dense matter have been a core interest of mine since I entered graduate school at Stony Brook in 1984. This interest was shaped both by the strong research activity on the subject at Stony Brook at the time and by the influence of Mannque Rho, who was a frequent visitor there. In this memoir dedicated to Mannque, I describe a selection of his works that sparked my interest in the subject and present my current perspective on what Mannque, together with Gerry Brown, sought to emphasize in the often-misinterpreted Brown--Rho scaling. In light of recent developments, I also discuss refinements of Brown--Rho scaling for mesons and baryons, associated with spontaneous chiral symmetry breaking and $U_A(1)$-breaking effects.
papers.reason: A memoir and technical perspective on hadron properties in dense matter, chiral symmetry breaking, and Brown-Rho scaling.

papers.title: Probing In-Medium Neutron-to-Dark-Fermion Conversion with Multimessenger Neutron Star Observations
papers.abstract: Neutron stars provide a natural environment for probing in-medium neutron-to-dark-fermion conversion and its impact on the dense-matter equation of state (EOS). We use multimessenger neutron star observations to map excluded and not-excluded regions of dark-sector parameter space for an EOS ensemble within a non-linear $\sigma$--$\omega$--$\rho$ relativistic mean-field (RMF) framework and determine their overlap across the ensemble. We include a fermionic dark component with repulsive self-interactions of strength $G_\chi$. We consider masses $m_\chi$ near the neutron mass and heavier states accessible in neutron star cores at sufficiently large neutron chemical potentials. To reduce sensitivity to the nucleonic EOS within this framework, we scan $m_\chi=939$--$1500$ MeV and $G_\chi=1$--$100$ fm$^2$ across 21 nucleonic EOSs: a main baseline set of 13 EOSs and soft and stiff limiting cases. Stellar sequences are tested against the requirement that the EOS support at least $2M_\odot$ neutron stars, GW170817 tidal-deformability bounds, and NICER mass--radius constraints, considering the Illinois--Maryland and X-PSI/Amsterdam inference sets separately. For the full ensemble of 21 EOSs, both NICER analyses identify similar regions excluded by all EOSs, with approximate minimum--maximum extents of $m_\chi=939$--$1300$ MeV and $G_\chi=1$--$11$ fm$^2$. Unlike the full 21-EOS ensemble, the main baseline set has a common not-excluded region whose extent depends on the NICER analysis. The soft and stiff limiting cases show how these regions shift when the nucleonic EOS predicts a maximum neutron star mass near $2M_\odot$ or large tidal deformabilities. Across these 21 calibrated nucleonic RMF EOSs, weak dark-sector repulsion is robustly disfavored across a broad dark-fermion mass range, while the extent of the remaining not-excluded region depends on the NICER analysis and baryonic EOS stiffness.
papers.reason: Uses multimessenger neutron star observations and relativistic mean-field equations of state to constrain in-medium neutron-to-dark-fermion conversion.

papers.title: Light top-flavoured dark matter in dark SMEFT: one-loop matching and phenomenology
papers.abstract: We study light top-flavoured dark matter (DM) below the electroweak (EW) scale within the dark Standard Model effective field theory (DSMEFT). We perform the one-loop matching of the DSMEFT onto the dark low-energy effective field theory (DLEFT) at the EW scale for all relevant operators that couple scalar, fermionic or vector DM, as well as axion-like particles, exclusively to third-generation quarks. After QCD evolution to the relevant low-energy scales, we match the DLEFT onto the non-relativistic EFT for DM-nucleus scattering. This EFT chain provides a unified framework for phenomenological studies of rare $B$- and $K$-meson decays with missing energy, direct and indirect detection, and the thermal relic abundance. Interpreting the Belle II excess in $B^+\to K^+\nu\bar\nu$ as a decay into DM, we find that only the DSMEFT operators contributing at tree level can accommodate it with $O(1)$ couplings for a new-physics scale of $1\,\mathrm{TeV}$. The decay $B^0\to K^{*0}+\mathrm{inv}$ provides the strongest constraint over large portions of the Belle II-favoured parameter space, while $K^+\to\pi^++\mathrm{inv}$ can dominate at low and $B_s\to\mathrm{inv}$, $B^+\to\pi^++\mathrm{inv}$ and $\Upsilon(1S)\to\mathrm{inv}$ become important at high DM masses, respectively. Direct-detection searches by CRESST-III and DarkSide-50 are competitive for operators involving scalar quark currents and, depending on the operator, exclude the Belle~II-favoured band for $m_{\mathrm{DM}}\gtrsim1$-$2\,\mathrm{GeV}$. We also perform detailed analyses of the thermal relic abundance and the indirect-detection constraints from the CMB and Fermi-LAT.
papers.topic: Top-Flavoured Dark Matter in Dark SMEFT
papers.reason: Performs one-loop matching of dark SMEFT to DLEFT for top-flavoured dark matter, connecting rare B/K decays, direct detection, and EFT chains.

papers.title: Exact flavor conservation at the quark level in causal clusters: strange particles, protons and light nuclei in small collision systems
papers.abstract: The suppression of strange hadrons in pp and p--Pb collisions at the LHC, including the $\phi$ meson, has recently been described by the exact conservation of strangeness imposed on the quarks of a causally connected cluster before hadronization. Here we extend this approach to the light flavors. The numbers of up and down quarks and antiquarks are conserved in the same cluster, and the suppression of a baryon or a nucleus depends only on how many light quarks of each flavor it contains. With the strangeness sector fixed by the previous analysis, a single constant, the ratio $r$ of light to strange quark abundances, determines the multiplicity dependence of protons, deuterons, He and hypertriton in pp and p--Pb collisions. Including the finite size of the nuclei, one obtains a very good fit of the data for $r=3.76\pm0.38$, i.e.\ strange quarks about 0.27 times as abundant as light quarks per flavor, close to the value known from string fragmentation
papers.topic: Exact Flavor Conservation in Small Systems
papers.reason: Extends causal cluster exact flavor conservation to light flavors to describe strangeness and light-quark hadron/nucleus suppression in pp and p-Pb collisions.

papers.title: LH$\mu$C: A high energy, high luminosity muon-hadron collider at CERN
papers.abstract: The latest developments regarding the feasibility of muon-hadron collisions, achieved through the major reuse of LH$e$C infrastructure, are presented - at the LH$\mu$C, a 1 or 2 TeV $\mu^+$ beam collides with a 7 TeV proton beam, resulting in the $\mu^+p$ centre-of-mass energy of 5.3 or 7.5 TeV, respectively, at an average luminosity close to $10^{34}$cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$. First, a concise scientific motivation is given, including exceptional prospects for neutrino science, and is followed by a presentation of the LH$\mu$C concept in a nutshell - from the source of ultra-cold anti-muons, through the muon booster, to the main muon ring. Basic considerations regarding the machine-detector interface and the general-purpose detector are also presented. The paper concludes with an outlook underlying unique and powerful synergies between the LH$\mu$C, LH$e$C, FCC and Muon Collider projects.
papers.reason: Examines the physics potential of the proposed LḦ̵̵́ΉC, highlighting exceptional prospects for neutrino science.

papers.title: Probing the singlet-triplet scotogenic model with lepton flavor violation, gravitational waves and dark matter
papers.abstract: We perform a comprehensive phenomenological analysis of neutrino masses, lepton-flavor violation, gravitational-wave signature induced by the first-order electroweak phase transition, and scalar dark matter within the framework of the singlet--triplet scotogenic model. We derive general analytical expressions for the one-loop Wilson coefficients of the penguin and box contributions to lepton-flavor-violating processes, considering generic scalar and fermion mediators. These general results are then applied to the singlet--triplet scotogenic model to calculate the branching ratios of $\mu\to e\gamma$ and $\mu\to e\overline{e}e$, as well as the coherent $\mu$--$e$ conversion rate. We systematically investigate the lepton-flavor-violation phenomenology and the constraints from current and future experiments. It is found that the coupling $\lambda_5$ plays a key role in connecting neutrino masses, lepton flavor violation, and dark matter direct detection. We also study the finite-temperature effective potential and the gravitational-wave signatures of the resulting first-order phase transition. By analyzing the thermal history of the model, we identify the viable parameter space allowing for a first-order electroweak phase transition in the early Universe and find that the portal parameters $\lambda_1^\Omega$ and $\mu_1$ play a crucial role in determining the transition strength. The corresponding stochastic gravitational-wave spectra can be probed by future gravitational-wave observatories. As a representative example, we identify a benchmark point that simultaneously satisfies the current constraints from lepton-flavor-violation and dark-matter experiments and generates a stochastic gravitational-wave spectrum that may be probed by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna, the Big Bang Observer, and the Ultimate Deci-hertz Interferometer Gravitational-wave Observatory.
papers.reason: Analyzes neutrino masses, lepton flavor violation, and dark matter within the singlet-triplet scotogenic model with gravitational wave signatures.

papers.title: Holographic Approaches to Hadron Structure
papers.abstract: We give an introduction to and an overview of holographic approaches to QCD and hadron structure. After an introduction to the string-theoretic foundations of holographic QCD, we review the predictions of top-down and bottom-up models for the phenomenology of mesons, baryons, and glueballs. We focus on the top-down model following from probe flavor branes in the Witten model of low-energy Yang-Mills theory and, in the more phenomenological approach of bottom-up models, on minimal models based on five-dimensional anti-de Sitter space.
papers.reason: Reviews top-down and bottom-up holographic approaches to QCD and hadron structure, including meson, baryon, and glueball phenomenology.

papers.title: Two-Particle Correlation Function in a Finite Volume
papers.abstract: We investigate the two-particle correlation function in a finite volume. First, defining an unphysical complex-energy sheet of the correlation function and identifying unstable states as poles on the sheet, we demonstrate that the expansion of the correlation function, which includes poles of unstable states, holds up to exponentially decreasing corrections with the volume size. Based on this result, we show that the finite-volume correction to the complex energy of the unstable state also decreases exponentially with the volume size, namely that finite-volume corrections are relatively small for the unstable states. Then, we show that the imaginary-time correlation function in a finite volume approaches that of the infinite volume as $\tau/L^2 \rightarrow 0$ while it is dominated by the lowest energy mode as $\tau/L^2 \rightarrow \infty$, where $\tau$ is the imaginary time, $L$ is the volume size. In drawing these conclusions, we first present a qualitative, general discussion and then demonstrate quantitative results using simple nonrelativistic models with a contact interaction (EFT) and a separable potential.
papers.reason: Analyzes two-particle correlation functions and unstable states in a finite volume, relevant to lattice QCD scattering analyses.

papers.title: Information geometry of continuum limits in lattice field theory: The Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions
papers.abstract: When the Boltzmann weight is nonnegative, the actions of a lattice field theory define a family of probability distributions that forms a statistical manifold, and its Fisher metric gives the number of measurements needed to distinguish two nearby actions. In the large-$N$ limit of the two-dimensional lattice Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions, we study the continuum limit, in which the lattice spacing $a$ is taken to zero with the mass gap $\Lambda$ fixed, through the Fisher metric of the distribution of the auxiliary field $\sigma$. The renormalization condition fixes an expectation coordinate, and dimensional transmutation becomes an exponential relation between it and a natural coordinate. The main result is that the $a\to0$ limits differ between the Fisher metric of the long-distance modes, whose momenta are fixed in physical units, and the Fisher metric of the full $P(\sigma)$. In the former, the lengths of the infinitely many irrelevant directions that change the kinetic term shrink, relative to the mass-term direction, to order $a\Lambda\log(1/(a\Lambda))$ or smaller, and when several modes are combined, only the two directions $(\Lambda,m)$ of the continuum theory remain. In the latter, the kinetic-term directions shrink at the same rate as the mass-term direction, and the difference in the regularization remains in correlations at distances of the order of the lattice spacing. An exception is the deformation that only adds a contact term to the propagator: as $a\to0$ its length goes to zero in both metrics, and it becomes indistinguishable from a change of the coupling $1/g^2$ (a lattice version of Kutasov's result). The curvature of the coupling plane at fixed kinetic term diverges as $(1/2)\log^2(1/(a\Lambda))$, not as the correlation volume often assumed in thermodynamic geometry, and the critical point is infinitely far in Fisher distance from any point at finite $a$.
papers.reason: Studies the continuum limit of the Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions using information geometry and the Fisher metric.

papers.title: Near-exact Upper Confidence Limits for Axion Haloscopes
papers.abstract: The data acquisition of axion haloscopes commonly implements sequential adaptive frequency scans. We present a method to calculate likelihood-based upper confidence limits on axion-photon coupling under this circumstance. We compare the likelihood-based method conceptually and quantitatively with tailor-made methods, i.e. the one proposed by Brubaker et al. (Geometric) and its upgrade the Bayesian Power-Measured (BPM) framework proposed by Palken et al. We find that the likelihood method yields average upper limits that are significantly more constraining than those obtained from these methods. For example, expected constraints improve by a factor of 1.4 as compared with the current state of the art when applied to projections for the ALPHA Plasma-haloscope. We further clarify the statistical basis for the Geometric and BPM methods. In particular, we point out the correspondence of BPM to e-values, proposed as an alternative to conventional p-values in statistics.
papers.reason: Presents a near-exact likelihood-based method to calculate upper confidence limits for axion haloscopes with sequential frequency scans.

papers.title: Negative-Power Density of States in Chiral-Orthogonal Disordered Systems and the IR Phase of QCD
papers.abstract: The recently discovered IR phase of QCD is characterized by an infrared (IR) sector of Dirac modes that separates and dynamically decouples from the bulk of the spectrum, becoming scale invariant in the process [1]. Among key features of this IR sector is the negative power-law behavior of Dirac spectral density near zero with power $p$ close to $-1$. Here we start investigating to what extent can this behavior be mimicked by chiral Anderson models. In particular, we study 3-D chiral-orthogonal systems with logarithmic off-diagonal disorder where negative-power ``spikes'' have been observed [2]. We find that at finite disorder strength $W$ of moderate strength, these models in fact do not have a power-singular density of states (DOS) at zero energy in the thermodynamic limit. Rather, this power $p_1$ vanishes and the spectrum features a very accurate power behavior with $p<0$ on an interval around $E = 1$ spreading increasingly closer to $E=0$ and $E = \infty$ with increasing $W$. We connect this to the fact that random hoppings $t$ in these quantum systems are drawn from a scale-invariant $1/t$ distribution regularized via $t \in [e^{-W/2}, e^{W/2}]$, and DOS with negative power can naturally arise inside that range. We show that $\lim_{W \to \infty} p(W, E)=-1$ for all energies accessible by our data. This indicates that, upon removing the cutoff $W$, quantum mechanics transforms the scale-invariant $1/t$ noise into a scale-invariant $1/E$ distribution of eigenstates, which mimics the interpretation of scale-invariant Dirac spectral densities in the IR phase as being due to scale-invariant glue backgrounds [1]. Our results imply that, to model the IR sector of the IR phase, the IR cutoff in chiral Anderson systems needs to be viewed as descending from the randomness strength $W$ rather than the lattice size $L$.
papers.reason: Studies chiral-orthogonal disordered systems and negative-power density of states to model the infrared phase and Dirac spectrum of QCD.

papers.title: Search for the rare decay $\eta^{\prime}\to 3\gamma$
papers.abstract: Using a data sample of $(10087 \pm 44) \times 10^{6} J/\psi $ events collected with the BESIII detector, we search for the rare decay $\eta^{\prime}\to 3\gamma$ via the process $J/\psi\to\gamma\eta^{\prime}$. No significant signal is observed and an upper limit on the branching fraction of $\eta^{\prime}\to 3\gamma$ is set at $\mathcal{B}(\eta^{\prime}\to 3\gamma) < 2.25\times 10^{-5}$ at the 90\% confidence level. This result improves the previous upper limit by more than a factor of four.
papers.reason: Reports an improved upper limit on the rare decay eta-prime to 3 gamma using BESIII data. [favorite author: Tao Han]

papers.title: First measurement of $\psi(3686)\to\bar{p} K^{+} \Sigma^{*}(1385)^{0} + c.c.$ and $\psi(3686)\to\bar{p} K^{*}(892)^{0} \Sigma^{+} + c.c.$
papers.abstract: Based on a sample of $(2712.4 \pm 14.3) \times 10^6$ $\psi(3686)$ events collected with the BESIII detector at the BEPCII collider, we report the first observation of the decays $\psi(3686)\to\bar{p} K^{+} \Sigma^{*}(1385)^{0}+c.c.$ and $\psi(3686)\to\bar{p} K^{*}(892)^{0} \Sigma^{+} + c.c.$. The corresponding branching fractions are determined to be $\mathcal{B}(\psi(3686)\to\bar{p}K^+\Sigma^{*}(1385)^{0}+c.c.)=(3.94\pm0.15_{\text{stat.}}\pm0.24_{\text{syst.}})\times10^{-5}$ and $\mathcal{B}(\psi(3686)\to\bar{p}K^{*}(892)^{0}\Sigma^++c.c.)=(4.93\pm0.14_{\text{stat.}}\pm0.30_{\text{syst.}})\times10^{-5}$. Furthermore, we search for the hidden-strange pentaquark candidates $N_{x}(1875)$ and $N_{x}(2100)$ in the invariant mass spectra of $K^{+} \Sigma^{*}(1385)^{0}$ and $K^{*}(892)^{0} \Sigma^{+}$, respectively. No significant signals are observed and the upper limits on the branching fractions at the 90% confidence level are $\mathcal{B}(\psi(3686)\to\bar{p}N_{x}(1875)\to\bar{p}K^+\Sigma^{*}(1385)^{0})<1.58\times10^{-6}$ and $\mathcal{B}(\psi(3686)\to\bar{p}N_{x}(2100)\to\bar{p}K^{*}(892)^{0}\Sigma^+)<3.09\times10^{-7}$.
papers.reason: Reports first measurements of specific psi(3686) decay branching fractions and searches for hidden-strange pentaquarks using BESIII data. [favorite author: Tao Han]

papers.title: A Tool-Grounded AI Agent for Gauge Coupling Unification and Proton Decay
papers.abstract: We present proton_agent, a tool-grounded AI agent that enables natural-language interaction with computational tools for gauge coupling unification and proton decay in grand unified theories. The agent translates user requests into computational tasks, selects and executes the appropriate tools, and interprets their outputs. All numerical calculations, model evaluations, experimental comparisons, parameter scans, and visualizations are handled by a deterministic scientific backend to ensure numerical accuracy and reproducibility. A central objective of this framework is to enable fully local deployment using free and open-source LLMs, while retaining compatibility with commercial LLM APIs. The framework computes one- and two-loop gauge beta coefficients for user-defined scalar and fermion multiplets and performs gauge coupling evolution through the Standard Model and various intermediate symmetry-breaking stages of $SO(10)$, including $SU(3)_C \times SU(2)_L \times SU(2)_R \times U(1)_{B-L}$, $SU(3)_C \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_R \times U(1)_{B-L}$, $SU(4)_C \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_R$, and $SU(4)_C \times SU(2)_L \times SU(2)_R$. For proton decay, the framework evaluates gauge-mediated dimension-six contributions in non-supersymmetric $SU(5)$ and $SO(10)$, as well as dressed dimension-five contributions in their supersymmetric counterparts. It supports benchmark calculations for user-specified parameter points, random and grid-based parameter scans, Markov-chain Monte Carlo exploration, comparisons with experimental limits, and publication-ready two- and three-dimensional visualizations. We describe the agent architecture, demonstrate its capabilities through representative benchmark calculations and regression tests, and discuss its current physics scope.
papers.topic: AI Agent for GUTs and Proton Decay
papers.reason: Presents a tool-grounded AI agent for gauge coupling unification and proton decay calculations, intersecting with physics workflow automation interests.

papers.title: Direct Detection of Millicharged Particles from Evaporating Primordial Black Holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the direct detection of millicharge particles produced via Hawking evaporation of neutral primordial black holes (PBHs). As they travel through the Galactic magnetic field and then Earth's overburden, they lose energy before reaching an underground detector. Using electron recoil signals, we obtain constraints on the mass and charge parameter space for XENONnT, JUNO and Super-K for evolved PBH populations with initial mass $ M_i=10^{15}~\rm g$ and $ M_i=8\times10^{15}~\rm g$ with initial abundances $f_i^{\rm PBH}=3.9\times10^{-7}$ and $f_i^{\rm PBH}=3.7\times10^{-4}$, respectively. In the relevant parameter space, this model can provide strong constraints in the high mass region.
papers.topic: Millicharged Particles from Primordial Black Holes
papers.reason: Computes direct detection constraints on millicharged particles produced via Hawking evaporation of primordial black holes using underground detector data.

papers.title: Dissecting flavor tagging with graph neural networks
papers.abstract: Graph neural networks such as ParticleNet are widely used for quark/gluon jet tagging. We study how the discriminating power of such a network is distributed between constituent multiplicity and the remaining structure of the jet, differentially in jet transverse momentum and multiplicity. To this end, we train ParticleNet on quark and gluon jets from Z+jet production in Pythia, with the two classes matched in transverse momentum and rapidity over the wide range $80\leq p_{T}^{\rm jet}\leq 400$ GeV. We find that the network learns how the fraction of gluon jets changes with the multiplicity in every $p_{T}^{\rm jet}$ bin, including the shift of the multiplicity at which quark and gluon jets are equally likely, which implies that it uses the jet scale (reconstructed from its constituents) jointly with its substructure. At fixed multiplicity, the gluon probabilities it assigns agree on average with the observed gluon fractions, but are widely spread about the mean.
